items.item_text: American Heart Association Basic Life Support (AHA BLS)
Graduate of an approved school of Communication Disorders holding a Master's degree or higher

Appropriately assesses patients of varying diagnoses and disorders requiring Speech Therapy according to established guidelines. Age range treated includes neonatal, pediatric, adolescent, adult, and geriatric. Staff will be assigned only age ranges for which they meet education, experience, and training.
CCS patients 0-21 years old will either be seen by CCS paneled therapists or have oversight by a CCS paneled therapist.
Assessment of swallowing/dysphagia, utilizing, but not limited to, bedside swallow and video swallow (MBSS) testing.
Establishes functional goals in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team based on the patient's rehabilitation potential.

Develops, implements, and modifies treatment plan in collaboration with interdisciplinary team to achieve goals. Utilizes evidence-based practice as available. Incorporates patient/family/Care Partner needs, interests, and goals in the development and execution of the treatment plan.

Provides patient/family/Care Partner/caregiver education, initiating as soon as feasible after admission. Works to ensure transfer of knowledge using a variety of techniques (i.e., teach-back, demonstration, video, written handouts).
Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology, within 24 months
Fire Safety, within 90 Days of start date.
